- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+), forecasts often overshoot and remain elevated longer than actual prices, which then correct downward.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values are trending downward.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 65–70.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to underestimation of downward corrections.
- When true values are trending upward, forecasts lag behind and underestimate the magnitude of the rise.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become more conservative — suggesting a delayed adjustment to recent trends.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward overestimating prices in the middle of the forecast window (days 15–25), especially after spikes.
- Forecasts often fail to account for mean reversion in the final 10 days, leading to persistent overestimation.
